title: The Pendulum's Period
subtitle: What decides how long one swing of a pendulum takes.
objectives: Set up a pendulum by its length and release angle.
Predict how the period changes with length.
Explain why the release angle and the mass do not change the period.

formulas.meaning: Period of a pendulum of length $L$ (small swings), with $g = 9.8\,\text{m/s}^2$.
Four times the length gives twice the period.

debrief: Only the length (and gravity) sets the period. A wider swing or a heavier bob takes the same time.

levels.title: Pull the bob back
levels.goal: Drag the bob to the right until the release angle is 20°, then check.
hints: Grab the purple bob in the picture and pull it sideways. The slider does the same thing.
The angle label next to the string shows the current value.

feedback.say: That is 20° to the left. Pull the bob to the right.

levels.solutionText: Pull the bob to the right until the label reads $\theta = 20°$.
levels.explain: The release angle is measured from the vertical line through the pivot.

levels.title: A slower swing
levels.goal: Change the string length so that one full swing takes 2.5 s (to within 0.05 s).
hints: A longer string swings more slowly.

feedback.say: The period is {T} s: too quick. Make the string longer.
The period is {T} s: too slow. Shorten the string.

levels.solutionText: $L = 9.8 \times (2.5 / 2\pi)^2 \approx 1.55\,\text{m}$, so a length of 1.5 m or 1.6 m is close enough.
levels.explain: The period grows with the square root of the length.

levels.title: Does the angle matter?
levels.goal: A 1 m pendulum released from 10° has a period of 2.01 s. What is its period when it is released from 20°? Try it out.
hints: Release it from 10° and from 20° and compare where the graph crosses zero.
Look at the formula: the angle does not appear in it.

feedback.say: Twice the angle does not mean twice the time: the bob also moves faster.

levels.solutionText: The period stays $2.01\,\text{s}$: for small swings it does not depend on the angle.
levels.explain: A wider swing covers more distance but at a higher speed, and the two effects cancel.

levels.title: Does the mass matter?
levels.goal: A 2 m pendulum with a 1 kg bob has a period of 2.84 s. The bob is replaced by a 4 kg bob. What is the period now?
hints: The mass is not one of them.

feedback.say: The mass does not appear in the formula for the period.

levels.solutionText: Still $2.84\,\text{s}$: the period does not depend on the mass.
levels.explain: A heavier bob is pulled harder by gravity but is also harder to move, so it swings in the same time.

levels.title: Build a clock
levels.goal: Old clocks use a pendulum that takes exactly 2.0 s for a full swing. Set up this pendulum (to within 0.03 s).
hints: Only one of the three controls changes the period.

feedback.say: The period is {T} s. Only the length changes it.

levels.explain: A pendulum about one metre long swings one way each second, which is why it was used in clocks.
